chips.name: GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU
chips.matrixUnit: 4th-gen Tensor Core (Ada Lovelace, AD107)
chips.interconnect: PCIe 4.0 x8
chips.notes: NVIDIA publishes only 233 AI TOPS (Ada 'AI TOPS' = FP8/INT8 with sparsity, FP16 accumulate), 3072 CUDA cores, 1470-2370 MHz boost and 35-115 W. Tensor/FP32 figures here are DERIVED at the 2370 MHz max boost using the Ada GeForce ratios from NVIDIA's whitepaper (dense INT8 = 233/2; FP8 and FP16/BF16 with FP32 accumulate = 1/4 and 1/8 of 233; TF32 = FP32 = 3072 x 2 x 2.37 GHz). FP16 with FP16 accumulate would be 58.3. Real clocks vary a lot by laptop TGP. FP64 is 1/64 of FP32 (CUDA guide throughput table). Bandwidth = 16 Gbps x 128-bit (Notebookcheck). Secondary: Notebookcheck (bandwidth).

chips.name: GeForce RTX 4090
chips.matrixUnit: 4th-gen Tensor Core (Ada Lovelace, AD102)
chips.interconnect: PCIe 4.0 x16 (no NVLink)
chips.notes: Dense figures from NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell whitepaper comparison table (which lists sparse as 2x). FP16/BF16/FP8 recorded with FP32 accumulate (GeForce runs these at half rate); with FP16 accumulate FP16 = 330.3 and FP8 = 660.6. FP64 = 1/64 of FP32 per CUDA guide throughput table (computed, NVIDIA does not print it).

chips.name: GeForce RTX 5090
chips.matrixUnit: 5th-gen Tensor Core (Blackwell, GB202)
chips.interconnect: PCIe 5.0 x16 (no NVLink)
chips.notes: Dense figures from NVIDIA RTX Blackwell whitepaper Appendix A (sparse = 2x; the 3352 'AI TOPS' on the product page is FP4 sparse). FP16/BF16/FP8 recorded with FP32 accumulate (half rate on GeForce); with FP16 accumulate FP16 = 419, FP8 = 838. FP6 is supported by 5th-gen Tensor Cores but NVIDIA's table gives no FP6 rate (null). FP64 = 1/64 of FP32 (computed).

chips.name: H100 SXM
chips.matrixUnit: 4th-gen Tensor Core (Hopper) + Transformer Engine
chips.interconnect: NVLink 4 900 GB/s; PCIe 5.0 x16 (128 GB/s)
chips.notes: NVIDIA page prints tensor figures 'with sparsity'; halved here (989/1979/1979/3958 sparse). TDP up to 700 W configurable.

chips.name: H200 SXM
chips.matrixUnit: 4th-gen Tensor Core (Hopper) + Transformer Engine
chips.interconnect: NVLink 4 900 GB/s; PCIe 5.0 x16 (128 GB/s)
chips.notes: Same Hopper die as H100 with more/faster memory. Vendor tensor figures are 'with sparsity'; halved here.

chips.name: B200 (HGX B200, per GPU)
chips.matrixUnit: 5th-gen Tensor Core (Blackwell) + 2nd-gen Transformer Engine
chips.interconnect: NVLink 5 1.8 TB/s per GPU; PCIe 6.0 x16 host
chips.notes: NVIDIA publishes HGX B200 as an 8-GPU board; per-GPU values = board / 8. Board: FP4 144|72 PF (sparse|dense), FP8/FP6 72 PF, INT8 72 POPS, FP16/BF16 36 PF, TF32 18 PF (all sparse; dense = 1/2), FP32 600 TF, FP64 296 TF, 1.4 TB; DGX B200 gives 1,440 GB and 64 TB/s total (-> 180 GB, 8 TB/s per GPU). TDP configurable up to 1000 W per GPU (HGX B200 PCF summary). Shipping late 2024. PCIe 6.0 host link is from general Blackwell knowledge, not verified on these pages.

chips.name: GB200 (per Blackwell GPU in the Grace Blackwell superchip)
chips.matrixUnit: 5th-gen Tensor Core (Blackwell) + 2nd-gen Transformer Engine
chips.interconnect: NVLink 5 1.8 TB/s per GPU (NVL72: 130 TB/s rack); NVLink-C2C to Grace CPU
chips.notes: Per-GPU = GB200 superchip / 2. NVIDIA's current GB200 NVL72 page lists per superchip (1 Grace + 2 Blackwell): FP4 40|20 PF (sparse|dense), FP8/FP6 20 PF, INT8 20 POPS, FP16/BF16 10 PF, TF32 5 PF (sparse; dense = 1/2), FP32 160 TF, FP64 80 TF, 372 GB HBM3e at 16 TB/s. Grace CPU: 72 Arm Neoverse V2 cores, up to 480 GB LPDDR5X at up to 512 GB/s, coherent with the GPUs over NVLink-C2C (NVIDIA quotes 900 GB/s for C2C on Grace Hopper; the GB200 page gives no C2C figure). Earlier NVIDIA material listed 384 GB / 192 GB per GPU; the page now says 372 GB. Per-GPU power is not published (null). Volume shipments 2025.

chips.name: GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip
chips.matrixUnit: 4th-gen Tensor Core (Hopper) + Transformer Engine
chips.interconnect: NVLink-C2C CPU-GPU 900 GB/s (coherent); NVLink 4 to other GPUs; up to 4x PCIe 5.0 x16
chips.notes: H100-class Hopper GPU + 72-core Grace CPU (Neoverse V2) on one module. Datasheet prints sparse | dense; dense used. Two memory options: 96 GB HBM3 at up to 4 TB/s (2023 launch) or 144 GB HBM3e at up to 4.9 TB/s (recorded). Plus up to 480 GB LPDDR5X at up to 512 GB/s on the CPU side (up to 624 GB fast memory total). Power configurable 450-1000 W for CPU + GPU + memory.

chips.name: DGX Spark (GB10 Grace Blackwell)
chips.matrixUnit: 5th-gen Tensor Core (Blackwell)
chips.interconnect: ConnectX-7 200 Gb/s (pair two Sparks); CPU-GPU via on-package C2C (no figure published)
chips.notes: NVIDIA quotes only 'up to 1 PFLOP FP4' using sparsity; dense FP4 = 500 TF (halved). FP32 31 TF is from NVIDIA's Hot Chips 2025 GB10 talk as reported by ServeTheHome (secondary). No official FP64/TF32/FP16/FP8/INT8 rates published (null). CPU: 20 Arm cores (10 Cortex-X925 + 10 Cortex-A725). 140 W is GB10 SoC TDP (CPU+GPU); box PSU 240 W. Also sold in 64 GB OEM configs. Secondary: ServeTheHome (fp32TF).

chips.name: Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit
chips.matrixUnit: 3rd-gen Tensor Core (Ampere), 32 Tensor Cores
chips.interconnect: none (embedded module; dev kit has M.2 PCIe slots and GbE)
chips.notes: 1024 CUDA cores, GPU up to 1020 MHz in 'Super' (MAXN SUPER) mode. NVIDIA headline 67 INT8 TOPS is sparse; dense 33 TOPS. NVIDIA lists '17 FP16 TFLOPs' without a sparse/dense label; it equals dense INT8/2, so taken as dense (moderate confidence). FP32 not published (approx 2.1 TF = 1024 x 2 x 1.02 GHz, not recorded). FP64 not published. PyTorch via NVIDIA's JetPack wheels (aarch64).

chips.name: Radeon 890M (Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 'Strix Point' iGPU)
chips.matrixUnit: WMMA on RDNA 3.5 (AI accelerators); separate XDNA 2 NPU
chips.interconnect: on-die (shares system memory with Zen 5 CPU and NPU)
chips.notes: 16 RDNA 3.5 CUs (gfx1150) at up to 2.9 GHz (AMD sales material also cites 3.0 GHz). GPU figures DERIVED, AMD does not print them: FP32 = 16 CU x 128 lanes x 2 (dual-issue) x 2.9 GHz; WMMA FP16/BF16/INT8 = 512 ops/clk/CU (RDNA3 rate, same as dual-issue FP16); FP64 = 1/16 of single-issue FP32 (= 1/32 of the dual-issue headline). Bandwidth = LPDDR5X-7500 x 128-bit (DDR5-5600 configs ~90 GB/s). NPU 50 INT8 TOPS (XDNA 2); whole SoC 'up to 80 TOPS'. Default TDP 28 W, cTDP 15-54 W. ROCm support for gfx1150 is limited/preview; check the ROCm compatibility matrix. Secondary: PC Gamer / TechPowerUp CPU DB (clock, TDP).

chips.name: Ryzen AI Max+ 395 'Strix Halo' (Radeon 8060S + XDNA 2 NPU)
chips.matrixUnit: WMMA on RDNA 3.5 (AI accelerators); separate XDNA 2 NPU
chips.interconnect: on-package (16 Zen 5 cores, GPU and NPU share LPDDR5X); PCIe 4.0 lanes for I/O
chips.notes: 40 RDNA 3.5 CUs (gfx1151) at up to 2.9 GHz. GPU figures DERIVED (AMD does not print GPU TFLOPS): FP32 = 40 x 128 x 2 (dual-issue) x 2.9 GHz; WMMA FP16/BF16/INT8 = 512 ops/clk/CU; FP64 = 1/16 single-issue FP32. Bandwidth = 8000 MT/s x 256-bit = 256 GB/s. Up to 128 GB; up to 96 GB can be assigned to the GPU on Windows (more on Linux). NPU 50 TOPS; AMD's 126 TOPS is the whole SoC. cTDP 45-120 W (AMD test configs often use 55 W). ROCm supports gfx1151 in recent releases. Power: AMD lists a 120 W TDP on the product page; laptops configure it between 45 and 120 W.

chips.name: Radeon RX 7900 XTX
chips.matrixUnit: WMMA (RDNA 3 'AI Accelerators', 2 per CU)
chips.interconnect: PCIe 4.0 x16
chips.notes: 96 CUs (gfx1100), 2.5 GHz boost. FP32 61.4 TF counts RDNA3 dual-issue; WMMA FP16/BF16/INT8 run at the same 2x rate (122.8). No sparsity, no FP8. FP64 = 1/32 of the dual-issue FP32 headline (1/16 single-issue), computed. amd.com could not be fetched during this research; figures from Tom's Hardware and Guru3D reprints of AMD's spec sheet (secondary).

chips.name: Radeon RX 9070 XT
chips.matrixUnit: WMMA (RDNA 4 2nd-gen AI Accelerators, structured sparsity)
chips.interconnect: PCIe 5.0 x16
chips.notes: 64 CUs (gfx1201), ~2.97 GHz boost. AMD's 1557 'AI TOPS' = INT4 with sparsity; dense FP16 matrix ~195 TF, FP8/INT8 389 (sparse 2x). Vector FP16 = 97.3 TF. FP64 = 1/16 of single-issue FP32, computed. Bandwidth = 20 Gbps x 256-bit (some listings say 644.6). amd.com could not be fetched; figures from Tom's Hardware review and GPUpoet/macmyths summaries of AMD's spec page (secondary).

chips.name: Instinct MI300X
chips.matrixUnit: Matrix Cores (MFMA, CDNA 3)
chips.interconnect: 7x Infinity Fabric links, 128 GB/s each (896 GB/s aggregate); PCIe 5.0 x16
chips.notes: 304 CUs (gfx942). ROCm docs give dense peaks (AMD marketing doubles FP16/FP8/INT8 'with sparsity'). FP32 matrix also 163.4. FP8 on MI300X is the FNUZ variant (E4M3FNUZ/E5M2FNUZ), not OCP FP8. 750 W TBP from Tom's Hardware report of AMD spec (secondary); 192 GB from ROCm specs table; IF link figures from AMD datasheet via search snippet.

chips.name: Instinct MI355X
chips.matrixUnit: Matrix Cores (MFMA, CDNA 4)
chips.interconnect: 7x Infinity Fabric links (>1 TB/s aggregate GPU-GPU); PCIe 5.0 x16
chips.notes: 256 CUs (gfx950), liquid-cooled OAM. Dense peaks from ROCm docs (sparse = 2x for FP16/BF16/FP8/INT8). MXFP6 and MXFP4 both 10 PF (AMD page rounds to 10.1). CDNA 4 drops hardware TF32 (null; emulated via BF16). Matrix FP64 = vector FP64 (78.6), i.e. half of MI300X's matrix FP64.

chips.name: Core Ultra 7 258V 'Lunar Lake' (Arc 140V + NPU 4)
chips.matrixUnit: XMX (Xe2) on Arc 140V; NPU 4 (Intel AI Boost)
chips.interconnect: on-package (CPU, GPU, NPU share memory)
chips.notes: Intel ARK: GPU 64 INT8 TOPS, NPU 47 TOPS, platform 115 TOPS; 8 Xe2 cores up to 1.95 GHz; 17 W base / 37 W max turbo. fp32TF and fp16TF are DERIVED: FP32 = 8 Xe-cores x 128 lanes x 2 x 1.95 GHz; XMX FP16 = INT8 TOPS / 2 (Xe2 XMX FP16 is half the INT8 rate). Bandwidth = 8533 MT/s x 128-bit. FP64 not published (null).

chips.name: Arc B580
chips.matrixUnit: XMX (Xe2 'Battlemage'), 160 engines
chips.interconnect: PCIe 4.0 x8
chips.notes: ARK: 20 Xe-cores, 2670 MHz, 233 INT8 TOPS (Intel's TOPS appear to use a ~2.85 GHz peak clock). fp32TF and fp16TF/bf16TF are DERIVED: FP32 = 20 x 128 x 2 x 2.67 GHz; XMX FP16/BF16 = INT8/2. FP64 rate not published by Intel (null). No FP8 in Xe2 XMX.

chips.name: Xeon 6980P (Xeon 6 'Granite Rapids', with AMX)
chips.matrixUnit: AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions: TMUL tiles), plus AVX-512 (2 FMA units)
chips.kernelLangs: C/C++ (AMX/AVX-512 intrinsics), OpenMP; torch.compile C++ codegen
chips.interconnect: 6x UPI 24 GT/s; 96 PCIe 5.0 lanes (CXL 2.0)
chips.notes: 128 cores, 2.0 GHz base / 3.2 GHz all-core / 3.9 GHz max turbo, 500 W. Intel publishes no FLOPS figures (all compute null). Rough theory, not recorded: AMX BF16 = 1024 FLOP/clk/core -> ~262 TF at 2.0 GHz (AMX clocks are lower in practice); AVX-512 FP64 = 32 FLOP/clk/core -> ~8 TF at 2.0 GHz. Bandwidth = 12 ch x 8800 MT/s x 8 B (MRDIMM); 614 GB/s with DDR5-6400. Granite Rapids adds AMX-FP16; AMX has no FP8/FP32.

chips.name: Gaudi 3 (HL-325L OAM)
chips.matrixUnit: MME (Matrix Multiplication Engine) x8 + 64 TPC vector cores
chips.blas: Intel Gaudi software (SynapseAI graph compiler, MME), TPC kernel library
chips.kernelLangs: TPC-C (custom TPC kernels); PyTorch eager/graph via habana_frameworks
chips.interconnect: 24x 200 GbE RoCE v2 on-chip (1.2 TB/s bidirectional); PCIe 5.0 x16
chips.notes: Whitepaper table is dense peak. MME: FP8 1835, BF16 1835, FP16 459, TF32 459, FP32 229 TF; TPC vector: BF16/FP16 28.7, FP32 14.3 (fp32TF records vector FP32). No FP64. INT8 not listed as an MME type. 900 W air-cooled OAM (up to 1.2 kW liquid); PCIe card 600 W. Source PDF is Intel's whitepaper hosted by a reseller (aspsys.com).

chips.name: RTX Spark (top configuration)
chips.matrixUnit: 5th-gen Tensor Core (Blackwell RTX GPU, up to 6,144 CUDA cores)
chips.notes: Windows-on-Arm superchip for laptops and small desktops, announced at Computex 2026, devices from fall 2026: Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 CUDA cores and a 20-core Grace CPU (built with MediaTek), up to 128 GB unified LPDDR5X; a smaller version has an 18-core CPU and up to 64 GB. NVIDIA quotes 'up to 1 petaflop FP4' without saying dense or sparse (DGX Spark's identical figure is with sparsity), so no FP4 rate is listed. NVIDIA publishes no memory bandwidth.

chips.name: M4
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5X unified memory (type per secondary sources; Apple says 'unified memory')
chips.matrixUnit: Neural Engine (16-core); Apple GPU (10-core, no dedicated matrix unit; simdgroup_matrix); SME (Scalable Matrix Extension) on the M4 CPU
chips.notes: CPU up to 10 cores (4P+6E), 10-core GPU, 28 billion transistors, second-gen 3 nm. Apple does not publish GPU TFLOPS; third-party databases give ~3.8-4.3 TFLOPS FP32 for the 10-core GPU depending on assumed clock (not used here). PyTorch MPS has no float64. The Neural Engine is reachable only through Core ML (not from PyTorch code).

chips.name: M4 Pro
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5X unified memory (type per secondary sources)
chips.matrixUnit: Neural Engine (16-core); Apple GPU (up to 20-core, no dedicated matrix unit; simdgroup_matrix); SME on the CPU
chips.notes: Up to 14-core CPU (10P+4E), up to 20-core GPU, Thunderbolt 5. Apple quotes 38 TOPS only for M4's 16-core Neural Engine; the M4 Pro/Max announcement gives no TOPS, so 38 is carried over from M4 (same 16-core design). No float64 on MPS.
chips.confidence: mixed (npuTOPS inferred from M4's figure; memory type secondary)

chips.name: M4 Max
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5X unified memory (type per secondary sources)
chips.matrixUnit: Neural Engine (16-core); Apple GPU (up to 40-core, no dedicated matrix unit; simdgroup_matrix); SME on the CPU
chips.notes: Up to 16-core CPU (12P+4E), up to 40-core GPU. Apple does not publish GPU TFLOPS; third-party databases give ~17 TFLOPS FP32 for the 40-core GPU (hmc-tech, nanoreview; not used). npuTOPS carried over from M4 (Apple gives no figure for Max). No float64 on MPS.
chips.confidence: mixed (npuTOPS inferred from M4's figure; memory type secondary)

chips.name: M3 Ultra
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5 unified memory (type per secondary sources)
chips.matrixUnit: Neural Engine (32-core, two dies); Apple GPU (up to 80-core, no dedicated matrix unit; simdgroup_matrix)
chips.notes: Two M3 Max dies joined by UltraFusion; 28- or 32-core CPU (up to 24P+8E), 60- or 80-core GPU. Apple gives no Neural Engine TOPS for M3 Ultra (secondary sources say ~36 TOPS = 2x M3's 18). Apple does not publish GPU TFLOPS; one third-party table gives ~28 TFLOPS FP32 for 80 cores (unsourced, not used). No SME on M3 (pre-M4 CPUs have Apple's undocumented AMX, used by Accelerate). No float64 on MPS.

chips.name: M5
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5X unified memory (LPDDR5X-9600 per secondary sources)
chips.matrixUnit: GPU Neural Accelerators (one per GPU core, 10) + Neural Engine (16-core); SME on the CPU
chips.kernelLangs: Metal (Metal 4 tensor APIs reach the Neural Accelerators)
chips.notes: Announced 14 Oct 2025. Up to 10-core CPU (4P+6E), 10-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in each core; Apple claims >4x peak GPU AI compute vs M4 but gives no TOPS/TFLOPS. Bandwidth 153 GB/s (~30% over M4). A '42 TOPS' Neural Engine figure circulates (Wikipedia, uncited); not used. No float64 on MPS.

chips.name: M5 Pro
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5X unified memory (type per secondary sources)
chips.matrixUnit: GPU Neural Accelerators (one per GPU core, up to 20) + Neural Engine (16-core); SME on the CPU
chips.notes: Announced 3 Mar 2026. 'Fusion Architecture' (two dies in one SoC). 18-core CPU (6 'super' + 12 performance cores), up to 20-core GPU. Apple claims >4x peak GPU AI compute vs M4 Pro; no TOPS/TFLOPS published. No float64 on MPS.

chips.name: M5 Max
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5X unified memory (type per secondary sources)
chips.matrixUnit: GPU Neural Accelerators (one per GPU core, up to 40) + Neural Engine (16-core); SME on the CPU
chips.notes: Announced 3 Mar 2026 (MacBook Pro), in Mac Studio from Aug 2026. 18-core CPU (6 super + 12 performance), up to 40-core GPU. Apple claims >4x peak GPU AI compute vs M4 Max; no TOPS/TFLOPS published. No float64 on MPS.

chips.name: M5 Ultra
chips.memoryType: LPDDR5X unified memory (type per secondary sources)
chips.matrixUnit: GPU Neural Accelerators (one per GPU core, up to 80) + Neural Engine (32-core)
chips.notes: Not in the original list; added because it is officially announced (25 Aug 2026, Mac Studio). Quad-die: two dual-die M5 Max joined by UltraFusion (>4.4 TB/s). Up to 36-core CPU (12 super + 24 performance), up to 80-core GPU. Apple quotes bandwidth as '1.2TB/s' (secondary sources: 1,228.8 GB/s). Apple's two newsroom posts give 4.3x and 4.5x peak GPU AI compute vs M3 Ultra. No TOPS/TFLOPS published.

chips.name: M6
chips.matrixUnit: GPU Neural Accelerators (one per GPU core, 12) + dual 16-core Neural Engine
chips.notes: Not in the original list; added because it is officially announced (Aug 2026, Mac mini). Apple's first 2 nm chip: 12-core CPU (2 super + 4 performance + 6 efficiency), 12-core GPU. Apple claims Neural Engine 'up to 2x the peak compute over previous generations' and GPU AI compute ~30% above M5; no TOPS/TFLOPS published. Drop this row if the table should stop at M5.

chips.name: Snapdragon X Elite (X1E-84-100)
chips.matrixUnit: Hexagon NPU (tensor/scalar/vector accelerators); Adreno X1-85 GPU (no dedicated matrix unit)
chips.blas: OpenBLAS, Arm Performance Libraries, KleidiAI (CPU); Qualcomm AI Engine Direct (QNN) / ONNX Runtime QNN EP for the NPU
chips.notes: 12 Oryon cores, 3.8 GHz all-core / 4.2 GHz dual-core boost, 4 nm. 'Up to 4.6 TFLOPs' Adreno GPU figure is Qualcomm's (precision not stated; FP32 assumed). PyTorch runs on the Arm64 CPU on Windows; the NPU runs compiled/quantized models through QNN/ONNX Runtime, not PyTorch code. NPU format list per Qualcomm Hexagon general docs, not this brief.

chips.name: Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme (X2E-96-100)
chips.matrixUnit: Hexagon NPU (64-bit NPU architecture); Adreno X2-90 GPU (no dedicated matrix unit)
chips.blas: OpenBLAS, Arm Performance Libraries, KleidiAI (CPU); Qualcomm AI Engine Direct (QNN) / ONNX Runtime QNN EP for the NPU
chips.notes: Announced Sep 2025, laptops H1 2026. 18 cores (12 Prime + 6 Performance), 4.4 GHz all-core, 5.0 GHz single/dual boost, 53 MB cache, 3 nm, Adreno X2-90 at 1.85 GHz. Qualcomm gives no GPU TFLOPS for X2. Some X2 Elite SKUs (X2E-90-100, X2E-84-100) are rated 85 TOPS. NPU runs compiled models via QNN, not PyTorch code.

chips.name: Cloud TPU v5e
chips.matrixUnit: MXU (systolic array): 1 TensorCore x 4 MXUs (128x128)
chips.notes: Dense per-chip peaks. ICI 400 GB/s bidirectional per chip. No FP64 on TPUs. MXU size 128x128 is per Google's TPU architecture docs (not on the v5e page fetched).

chips.name: Cloud TPU v6e (Trillium)
chips.matrixUnit: MXU (systolic array): 1 TensorCore x 2 MXUs (256x256) + SparseCore
chips.notes: Dense per-chip peaks. ICI 800 GB/s bidirectional (4 ports). FP8 not listed on Google's v6e page. No FP64.

chips.name: TPU7x (Ironwood)
chips.matrixUnit: MXU (systolic array): 2 TensorCores + 4 SparseCores per chip
chips.notes: Announced Apr 2025; TPU7x GA per Cloud TPU release notes. Dense per-chip peaks. ICI 1,200 GB/s bidirectional (6 links x 200 GB/s). Pods up to 9,216 chips. Per-chip power and MXU count not published on the docs page. No FP64.

chips.name: Trainium2
chips.matrixUnit: NeuronCore-v3 (8 per chip; systolic Tensor Engine)
chips.blas: Neuron compiler (neuronx-cc) via PyTorch (torch-neuronx / TorchNeuron), JAX
chips.notes: Dense per-chip peaks; TF32 also 667 TFLOPS. Sparse (FP8/FP16/BF16/TF32) 2,563 TFLOPS. NeuronLink-v3 1.28 TB/s per chip. torch-neuronx historically exposed the chip as an XLA device ('xla'); AWS's newer native TorchNeuron backend uses 'neuron'. Power not published.

chips.name: Trainium3
chips.matrixUnit: NeuronCore-v4 (8 per chip)
chips.blas: Neuron compiler via PyTorch (TorchNeuron / torch-neuronx), JAX
chips.notes: Announced Dec 2025 (re:Invent). fp8TF is MXFP8 (MXFP4 same 2,517 TFLOPS). The Neuron docs also list a 'sparse FP16/BF16/TF32' row of 2,517 TFLOPS, so the labelling is slightly ambiguous; 2,517 MXFP8 is treated as dense. NeuronLink-v4 2.56 TB/s per chip. UltraServer: 144 chips, 362 MXFP8 PFLOPS.

chips.name: Raspberry Pi 5 (BCM2712)
chips.matrixUnit: none (4x Cortex-A76 NEON SIMD; VideoCore VII GPU)
chips.kernelLangs: C/NEON intrinsics, Vulkan 1.3 compute (GPU, not usable from PyTorch)
chips.notes: Quad Cortex-A76 at 2.4 GHz, 512 KB L2/core, 2 MB L3; VideoCore VII GPU (OpenGL ES 3.1, Vulkan 1.3); PCIe 2.0 x1. PyTorch can't use the GPU: CPU only. powerW is the 5V/5A USB-C supply rating, not a measured draw. Raspberry Pi publishes no bandwidth or FLOPS; derived estimates: ~17 GB/s (32-bit LPDDR4X-4267) and ~0.15 TFLOPS FP32 CPU peak (4 cores x 16 FLOP/cycle x 2.4 GHz), not filled in.

chips.name: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ (Hailo-8L, 13 TOPS)
chips.matrixUnit: Hailo-8L dataflow NPU
chips.notes: Connects over Raspberry Pi 5's PCIe Gen 3 interface. Runs models exported (ONNX/TFLite) and compiled with the Hailo Dataflow Compiler to .hef, not PyTorch code; integrated with rpicam-apps/Picamera2. Launch price $70. Same spec as the earlier AI Kit. powerW is Hailo's typical figure for the Hailo-8L chip, not the whole HAT. INT4 weights per Hailo general docs (secondary).

chips.name: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ (Hailo-8, 26 TOPS)
chips.matrixUnit: Hailo-8 dataflow NPU
chips.notes: PCIe Gen 3 to Raspberry Pi 5. Compiled models only (Hailo Dataflow Compiler, .hef). Launch price $110. powerW is Hailo's typical figure for the Hailo-8 chip.

chips.name: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ 2 (Hailo-10H)
chips.matrixUnit: Hailo-10H dataflow NPU
chips.blas: none; HailoRT runtime, hailo-ollama for LLMs
chips.notes: Launched 15 Jan 2026 at $130 (product page now lists $200). 8 GB onboard RAM lets it run LLMs/VLMs up to ~6B parameters (launch models ~1-1.5B: Llama 3.2 1B, Qwen2.5 1.5B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill 1.5B). Compiled models only; the Dataflow Compiler also compiles LoRA adapters. powerW is Hailo's typical figure for the Hailo-10H chip.

chips.name: RK3588 board (Radxa ROCK 5B)
chips.matrixUnit: RKNPU (3-core NPU); Mali-G610 MP4 GPU (no matrix unit); 4x Cortex-A76 + 4x Cortex-A55
chips.blas: OpenBLAS, Arm Performance Libraries, KleidiAI (CPU); RKNN runtime (NPU)
chips.kernelLangs: OpenCL (Mali GPU), Vulkan, none for NPU (RKNN-Toolkit2 compiles models)
chips.notes: 8 nm; A76 up to 2.4 GHz, A55 up to 1.8 GHz. NPU runs models converted with RKNN-Toolkit2 (from ONNX/PyTorch export/TFLite), not PyTorch code; PyTorch uses the CPU only. Rockchip/Radxa publish no GPU GFLOPS or memory bandwidth (derived ~34 GB/s for 64-bit LPDDR4X-4224, not filled).

chips.name: Coral USB Accelerator (Edge TPU)
chips.memoryType: none (on-chip SRAM only; uses host memory)
chips.matrixUnit: Edge TPU (systolic MXU-style ASIC)
chips.kernelLangs: none (Edge TPU Compiler on full-integer-quantized TFLite)
chips.notes: USB 3.0 Type-C. 2 TOPS per watt (so ~2 W at peak). Models must be full-integer quantized TFLite, compiled with the Edge TPU Compiler; no PyTorch support (PyTorch models need conversion to TFLite). coral.ai currently redirects to an appspot mirror.

chips.name: Graviton4
chips.matrixUnit: none (96x Neoverse V2, 4x128-bit SVE2 per core with BF16/INT8 matrix-multiply instructions)
chips.blas: OpenBLAS, Arm Performance Libraries, KleidiAI, oneDNN (ACL)
chips.notes: Announced Nov 2023, GA Jul 2024. 96 Neoverse V2 cores, 2 MB L2/core. bandwidthGBs derived from 12 x DDR5-5600 x 8 B (widely quoted as 536.7 GB/s); AWS's own post gives channels, not GB/s. Derived FP64 peak ~4.3 TFLOPS (96 x 16 FLOP/cycle x ~2.8 GHz), not filled. Graviton5 (192 cores) has been announced by AWS.
chips.confidence: mixed (bandwidthGBs derived from vendor channel count/speed)

chips.name: Grace CPU (C1, single CPU)
chips.matrixUnit: none (72x Neoverse V2, 4x128-bit SVE2 per core with BF16/INT8 matrix-multiply instructions)
chips.blas: NVPL (NVIDIA Performance Libraries), Arm Performance Libraries, OpenBLAS, KleidiAI
chips.notes: 72 Neoverse V2 cores, 114 MB L3. Bandwidth is up to 512 GB/s for 120/240 GB and up to 384 GB/s for the 480 GB option. powerW: C1 configurable 140-250 W for CPU + LPDDR5X; Grace CPU Superchip (144 cores) 500 W. In GH200/GB200 the Grace is paired with a GPU (PyTorch 'cuda' runs on the GPU). FP64 peak not published; derived ~3.5 TFLOPS at ~3.1 GHz, not filled.

chips.name: Ascend 910B
chips.matrixUnit: Da Vinci AI Core: 1 cube (matrix) unit + 2 vector units per core; 20-25 active AI cores depending on SKU
chips.blas: CANN aclnn operator library, CANN ops (math/NN operator repos)
chips.notes: Figures from CSET's analysis (not a Huawei datasheet). ~400 FP16 TFLOPS is CSET's figure for the top 910B SKU; it lists 910B3 at 313 and 910B4 at 280 TFLOPS. 64 GB / 1600 GB/s applies to 910B1-910B3 (four 16 GB HBM2e stacks); 910B4 has 32 GB / 800 GB/s. L2 192 MB. Process believed to be SMIC 7nm (N+2), not confirmed. Year: CSET calls 910B the second generation; 2023 is the commonly cited volume year. INT8 and power not given by CSET.

chips.name: Ascend 910C
chips.matrixUnit: Two co-packaged dies; per die 24 AI cube (AIC) cores for matrix math + 48 AI vector (AIV) cores
chips.blas: CANN aclnn operator library, CANN ops (math/NN operator repos)
chips.notes: From Huawei's own CloudMatrix384 paper (arXiv 2506.12708 v1, Sec. 3.3.1): ~376 dense BF16/FP16 TFLOPS per die, 752 per package; 1,054 INT8 (paper writes 'TFLOPS'); eight 16 GB on-package memory stacks = 128 GB; 1.6 TB/s per die, 3.2 TB/s per package; die-to-die 540 GB/s; UB scale-up 392 GB/s bidirectional per die; RDMA 200 Gbps per die. The paper says 'memory stacks' without naming the HBM generation. No FP8 in hardware on 910-series (FP8 arrives with Ascend 950). Power not stated.

chips.name: Ascend 950PR
chips.matrixUnit: Ascend 950 die (shared with 950DT); vector units combine SIMD and SIMT; memory access granularity 128 B (down from 512 B)
chips.notes: Roadmap figures from Huawei Connect 2025 keynote (announced Sep 2025, launch Q1 2026, for prefill and recommendation). 1 PFLOPS in FP8/MXFP8/HiF8; 2 PFLOPS MXFP4 (no FP4 field here). Formats listed for the 950 series: FP32, HF32, FP16, BF16, FP8, MXFP8, HiF8, MXFP4, HiF4. Interconnect 2 TB/s. Memory capacity and bandwidth not stated on the keynote page (third-party reports cite 128 GB at 1.6 TB/s; not used). BF16/FP16 rates not stated.

chips.name: Ascend 950DT
chips.matrixUnit: Ascend 950 die (shared with 950PR); vector units combine SIMD and SIMT
chips.notes: Roadmap figures from Huawei Connect 2025 keynote; launch Q4 2026, for decode and training. 1 PFLOPS FP8, 2 PFLOPS FP4; 144 GB at 4 TB/s; interconnect 2 TB/s. Differs from 950PR only in memory subsystem and timing.

chips.name: Ascend 960
chips.notes: Roadmap (planned Q4 2027): 2 PFLOPS FP8, 4 PFLOPS FP4; adds HiF4 format. Huawei says twice the 950's compute, memory bandwidth, memory capacity and interconnect ports, but gives no absolute memory figures.

chips.name: Ascend 970
chips.notes: Roadmap (planned Q4 2028), specs still being finalised per Huawei: 4 PFLOPS FP8, 8 PFLOPS FP4; interconnect 4 TB/s; memory bandwidth at least 1.5x the 960's.

chips.name: MLU370-X8
chips.matrixUnit: MLUarch03 MLU cores (two MLU370 chiplet dies on the card)
chips.notes: All numbers from Cambricon's MLU370-X8 product page. Also INT16 128 TOPS; MLU-Link 4 ports, 200 GB/s aggregate bidirectional; PCIe Gen4 x16; 250 W max, passive cooling. 7nm chiplet design. Siyuan 370 chip launched Nov 2021; the X8 card followed (2022). No FP8.

chips.name: MLU590
chips.notes: Cambricon has not published a 590 datasheet. 80 GB HBM2e per card from a Chinese tech article quoting a procurement-style spec (8-card server >= 640 GB, >= 16,384 GB/s aggregate, implying ~2 TB/s per card, not used). Precisions listed there: FP32, TF32, BF16, FP16, INT16, INT8, INT4. Process reported as SMIC N+2 (7nm-class). Per-card compute unpublished; press comparisons ('~80% of A100', '80-90% of H100') disagree and are not used. Year from aiwiki.

chips.name: MTT S4000
chips.matrixUnit: Third-gen MUSA architecture (Quyuan) with tensor cores: TF32/FP16/BF16/INT8 tensor supported
chips.kernelLangs: MUSA C (CUDA-like; MUSIFY ports CUDA source)
chips.notes: Vendor product page gives 48 GB, 768 GB/s, Max TGP 450 W, PCIe 5.0 x16, MTLink 240 GB/s inter-card; it lists FP32/TF32/FP16/INT8 tensor only as 'Supported' with no rates. GDDR6 (384-bit, 16 Gbps) is from press/TechPowerUp, consistent with 768 GB/s. Press widely reports ~25 TFLOPS FP32 and ~200 TOPS INT8 (Dec 2023 launch), not entered because I could not open a page stating them. No FP8.

chips.name: MTT S5000
chips.matrixUnit: Fourth-gen MUSA 'PingHu' architecture (PH100 chip); hardware-native FP8 tensor; FP8 through FP64 supported
chips.notes: Vendor product page confirms PingHu architecture, OAM module, native FP8 and FP8-FP64 support but publishes no numbers. 80 GB, 1.6 TB/s and ~1 PFLOPS FP8 come from a Moore Threads disclosure (Feb 2026) as carried by MyDrivers and aggregated by flopper.io; one report says 1024 TFLOPS. Inter-card ~784 GB/s reported in Chinese press (not entered). Memory type (HBM generation) unconfirmed.

chips.name: Zhenwu 810E (PPU)
chips.blas: PPU SDK libraries with cuBLAS / cuDNN / cuSolver / NCCL-compatible interfaces
chips.kernelLangs: CUDA-compatible C++ (PPU SDK exposes CudaRT-compatible API)
chips.notes: Alibaba Cloud ACK docs (PPU page): TDP 400 W, OAM, PCIe 5.0 x16, HBM2e 96 GB, 2765 GB/s, ICN inter-chip 700 GB/s (seven ports; not memory bandwidth). No compute rates published; press says comparable to NVIDIA H20. Year: T-Head publicly listed the chip in Jan 2026 (TrendForce), though it was already deployed in Alibaba Cloud clusters. PyTorch device name not stated in the docs; given the CUDA-compatible runtime it presumably presents as 'cuda', but unverified, so null.

chips.name: BR100
chips.matrixUnit: T-core tensor engine in each EU (16 EUs per SPC); tensor types FP32, TF32+, BF16, INT16, INT8, INT4; 3D MMA
chips.blas: BIRENSUPA libraries (names not given on the slides)
chips.notes: From Biren's Hot Chips 34 (2022) slides: 1074 mm2 over two 7nm chiplets, 77 B transistors, 2048 TOPS INT8, 1024 TFLOPS BF16, 512 TFLOPS TF32+ (Biren's 1+8+10-bit format, reuses the BF16 multiplier), 256 TFLOPS FP32 (slide headline, likely via tensor path), 64 GB HBM2e, 8 BLink ports with 2.3 TB/s external I/O, PCIe Gen5 x16 with CXL, OAM 550 W. FP16 listed only as 'also supported'. Memory bandwidth not on the slides (press reports ~1.64 TB/s; not entered). Shipping parts may be cut-down (BR104 / BR100P).

chips.name: P800
chips.matrixUnit: XPU-P architecture (details unpublished)
chips.notes: Only firm number: 345 FP16 TFLOPS (TechInsights; also a Guosen Securities report via 36Kr). TechInsights calls it the third-generation Kunlun part (Kunlun 2: 128 FP16 TFLOPS) with dual-sourced 2.5D packaging. Kunlunxin markets 8-bit inference support and an 8-card server running DeepSeek-V3/R1 671B. Memory capacity/bandwidth, power and year not found on a page I could open (kunlunxin.com returned 403). Software: tight PaddlePaddle integration; PyTorch adapter name not verified.

chips.name: C600
chips.matrixUnit: XCORE 1.5 ISA tensor instructions incl. FP8 / BF8 and FP4 conversion
chips.blas: MXMACA libraries (mcBLAS / mcDNN names not verified)
chips.notes: Unveiled WAIC 27 Jul 2025. 144 GB HBM3e per TrendForce; MetaX's own page avoids capacity, bandwidth and compute figures, saying only that single-card compute exceeds NVIDIA H20. 1.0 kW is MetaX's stated maximum board power (via flopper.io, citing metax-tech.com). A 3.6 TB/s figure in TrendForce's article belongs to Enflame's L600, not C600, so bandwidth is null. FP8 supported (no rate).

chips.name: Tiangai 100 (BI-V100)
chips.matrixUnit: General-purpose GPU architecture
chips.notes: Official product page: 32 GB HBM2, 250 W board power, PCIe Gen4 x16, passive cooling; released March 2021 (company homepage). No compute or memory-bandwidth figures on the official page. Newer Tiangai 150 / 300 have product pages but no spec numbers were retrievable (a generic '64 GB HBM, 350 W' appears unattributed to a model). PyTorch device name not stated officially (stack is marketed as compatible with mainstream ecosystems; 'cuda' likely but unverified).

chips.name: DCU K100 (Shensuan)
chips.nameZh: 海光 深算 DCU K100
chips.blas: DTK hipBLAS / rocBLAS-derived, MIOpen-derived DNN library, RCCL-derived collectives
chips.notes: Placeholder: hygon.cn product pages did not render for me, so no official numbers are entered. Hygon's DCU is a GPGPU in the ROCm/HIP lineage, programmed through Hygon's DTK (DCU Toolkit); PyTorch builds for HIP reuse the torch.cuda interface and the 'cuda' device string (PyTorch docs). Library names reflect the ROCm lineage and are not confirmed from a Hygon page.

chips.name: L600
chips.notes: Placeholder: enflame-tech.com returned 403, so no official numbers are entered. Press (TrendForce, WAIC Jul 2025) calls L600 Enflame's fourth-generation chip with 144 GB memory, 3.6 TB/s and FP8 support. Earlier S60 inference card (2024, third-gen 'Suisi 320' architecture) is reported in a third-party test report with 48 GB GDDR6, 672 GB/s, 300 W. Neither is vendor-confirmed here.
